body_markdown:
Paul Newman is most widely known for his incredible filmography. Whether it was drama or comedy, he was able to inhabit a range of characters with careful nuance and, when necessary, his amazing charisma. Despite his Academy Award–winning film career, those who knew the actor, director, and philanthropist best might first describe him as a driver. Although Newman didn’t really focus on racing until he was in his mid-40s, his passion for wheel-to-wheel competition kept him in the driver’s seat until he was in his 80s.


With four SCCA Trans Am championships and a class win at Le Mans in a Porsche 935, it’s tough to pin down Newman’s most impressive feat behind the wheel. One of his top achievements, however, has to be the Rolex 24 Hours of Daytona class win he secured in a Roush Mustang Cobra with co-drivers Tommy Kendall, Mark Martin, and Michael Brockman.


At the time, Mark Martin had only won the first of his five IROC championships. His long NASCAR Cup Series partnership with Roush Racing saw him finish second in points four times, coming frustratingly close to beating Dale Earnhardt for the series win in 1990. Tommy Kendall had already proven himself in IMSA GT racing and had even been called upon to take the reins for a few NASCAR Cup road races, including a Sears Point race where he famously battled Mark Martin.


Roush Performance


The Mustang Cobra racked up 682 laps at Daytona to finish third overall, just eight laps behind the outright winner and 27 laps ahead of its next-closest competitor. The win marked several milestones: It was the 10th class win at Daytona for Roush Racing, with wins every year the team competed beginning in 1985 (Roush did not compete in 1994). The car’s number 70 also marked Paul Newman’s age, as he’d celebrated his 70th birthday just over a week prior. The class victory made Newman the oldest driver to win a major sanctioned race. This winning Roush Mustang Cobra[recently sold at Mecum’s Nashville event](https://www.mecum.com/lots/1173896/1995-ford-mustang-cobra-nobodys-fool-imsa-road-race-car/?aa_id=785462-0) for $935,000.


Mecum


Mecum


While the car uses a tube chassis and doesn’t have much factory Mustang DNA, its composite bodywork still looks like the last of the pushrod-powered Mustang Cobras. Its 6.0-liter Roush V-8 produces somewhere in the neighborhood of 650 horsepower and routes it all to the rear axle by way of a five-speed manual transmission.


This Mustang Cobra has all of the hallmarks of a highly collectible race car. Beyond the class win itself, it earned the last of 10 straight Daytona class victories from a legendary team owner and race car builder. In fact, other than Carroll Shelby, few individuals are more synonymous with Ford racing than Jack Roush. The talent who piloted the car were some of the top road racers of their generation, with IMSA, IROC, and Trans Am championships all to their names. The fact that one of those Trans Am champions was also one of America’s favorite Hollywood stars makes it even more incredible.


In addition to the race-worn body panels that show all of the scars you’d expect a race-winning Mustang to accumulate when driving more than 2400 miles, the sale included this fresh set of body panels, ready for the car’s next track outing.


Mecum


A contemporary Mustang road race car, campaigned by Tommy Kendall in the 1997 SCCA Trans Am series,[also sold at the same Mecum event, for $825K.](https://www.mecum.com/lots/1173897/1997-ford-mustang-cobra-scca-trans-am-road-race-car/?aa_id=785465-0) Kendall absolutely dominated the competition that season, breaking Mark Donohue’s 1968 record for eight consecutive wins in Roger Penske’s Sunoco Chevrolet Camaro by piloting his Roush Mustang to 11 straight checkered flags. While Kendall’s Mustang represents an amazing feat of driving and engineering, one that still hasn’t been bested 30 years later, the combination of class-winning provenance and star power made Newman’s the must-have Mustang.


In addition to its link to racing royalty, the Mustang also gives the current owner the opportunity to participate in vintage racing. Some of Paul Newman’s former Brock Racing Enterprises Datsuns are staples at the Rolex Monterey Motorsports Reunion at Laguna Seca. Hopefully, this racing legend will make it back out on the tarmac soon.
